purpose: Omadacycline is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (a lung infection you catch outside of a hospital) and skin infections. Your doctor may prescribe it when other antibiotics are not a good fit for you. It works against a wide range of bacteria that can cause these types of infections.
how_it_works: Omadacycline works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to survive and grow. Think of it like pulling the plug on the bacteria's factory — without those proteins, the bacteria cannot multiply and your immune system can clear the infection. It is specially designed to work even against some bacteria that have become resistant to older antibiotics.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and headache. Some people notice an upset stomach, especially with the IV form. These effects are usually mild and tend to improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you are pregnant, as it can harm the developing baby and affect bone and tooth development. Avoid it if you are breastfeeding. Like all antibiotics, it can sometimes cause a serious gut infection called C. difficile — call your doctor if you develop severe or persistent diarrhea. This medicine can also make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so use sunscreen and avoid prolonged sun exposure while taking it.
typical_dosing: For pneumonia, a common dose is 100 mg given once a day, either by IV in a hospital or by mouth as a tablet at home. For skin infections, dosing may start higher on the first day and then continue once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, take all doses as directed, and finish the full course even if you feel better early.
